title: Backdraft shift notes — pocket draft
content:
Purpose: pocket-size, noisy, informal handoff for small/medium incidents. Not authoritative; use official runbook for escalations > Sev2.

Start-of-shift checklist (5–10m):
- Slack presence: update status to \"on-call: backdraft\" in #oncall. Post a short intro if this is your first shift.
- Pager review: skim the last 6 hours of alerts (PagerDuty/ops-alerts). Note recurring alerts and whether they were paged or suppressed.
- Dashboard glance: open Console -> Per-route latency (last 1h), error rate (5m), and token cost. Look for spikes >2x baseline.
- Capacity snapshot: query `rbw capacity show --pool inference-main` (or Console > Dedicated -> pools). Check utilization >80%? if yes, note to watch for queueing.
- KV cache health: quick check `redis-cli -h kv-cache-redis INFO` and check hit_ratio if available (custom metric: `redwood.kv_cache.hit_ratio`).

Common triage steps (first 10–30m for a new active incident):
1) Narrow scope: Which routes/models are impacted? Use per-route view; filter by model tag (e.g., `gptx-8q`).
2) Reproduce: run a small live request from the CLI (`rbw request --route chat --input \"hello\" --region us-west1`) to see latency and errors.
3) Logs: `rbw logs tail --route <route> --since 10m`. Search for OOM, CUDA errors, or kernel failures.
4) Fallback: if model worker pool is overloaded, flip routing policy to allow variant fallback: Console -> Routing -> edit policy -> enable \"allow-variant-fallback\". Note: this may change token cost; communicate in Slack.
5) Short-term mitigation: increase burst capacity (+10%) or restart a stuck worker (see below).

Quick commands I actually use: (copy-paste but check flags)
- Check queue length: `rbw metrics query \"inference.queue.length{pool=\\\"inference-main\\\"}\" --last 5m`
- Restart worker on host: `ssh s-re@worker-23 && sudo systemctl restart redwood-inference-worker` (only restart if logs show stuck loop or kernel crash).
- Evict KV entries for a problematic model: `rbw kv purge --prefix model/gptx-8q/prefix-` (light touch; coordinate with product if persistent).
- Force canary rollback: `rbw rollout rollback --canary-id CANARY-551`

Escalation and contacts (fast):
- First escalate to SRE lead (call): Alex Rivera (pager)
- GPU/infra contact (if node-level): On-call infra (channel #infra-oncall) -> paged via PagerDuty
- Applied ML (model behavior regressions): Samir Patel (Slack @sps)
- Security/PII concerns: stop requests, escalate to security@redwood immediately (no public comms).

Notes on weird recurring things I've seen this quarter:
- Intermittent latency spikes correlated with long-sequence Chat completions (seq > 1024). Root cause often batching policy not respecting priority; shortfix: adjust `max_batch_latency_ms` lower for high-priority route.
- Model variant mismatch: sometimes routing sends a quantized variant that lacks a plugin; causes 500 errors. Workaround: pin route to explicit model_version until we patch the variant registry.
- KV cache thrash after deploy: cache keys get invalidated causing sudden load to origin; watch `redwood.cache.miss_spike` metric after rollouts.

Temporary procedures (do not commit to infra automation without review):
- If worker process shows `CUDA out of memory` repeatedly across multiple nodes, and we need immediate relief: scale pool by +1 host, increase node-level swap file (only if test-approved), and schedule deeper debugging. Log decisions in #oncall with evidence.
- For a noisy low-priority route causing global batching delays: set route throttle `max_parallel_requests=2` for 30 minutes and monitor.

Handoff template (what I leave for the next person):
- What I did: short bullets of actions taken (restarts, rollbacks, temporary throttles).
- Open things: tickets, follow-ups, who to ping (names & PR links).
- Current status: green/yellow/red, with a note about instability windows.
- Next check-in: if still unstable, escalate to SRE lead within 30m.

Personal reminders / notes to self:
- When restarting workers, watch for orphaned processes: `ps aux | grep inference-worker` and ensure old processes exit.
- Be conservative with KV purge; avoid wide prefixes during US business hours.
- If you toggle \"allow-variant-fallback\", announce in #oncall and include expected cost delta.

Open questions I'm leaving in this draft (follow-ups):
- Can we add a per-route \"emergency-throttle\" toggle in Console to avoid editing policy JSON mid-incident? (Ticket: JIRA-9876)
- Investigate whether batching latency config should be route-aware by default (some routes always need low latency).

Random scratch (do not rely on this):
- snippet: `rbw debug heatmap --route chat --range 1h | grep slow-path`
- mental note: when in doubt, snapshot logs + metrics and create a single summary in the incident thread — helps postmortem clarity.

End-of-shift handoff quick bullets (what I actually write to the incoming oncall):
- baseline: CPU/GPU util at 62/73%, queue length 12 (normal <20), no active alerts.
- actions: restarted worker-23 due to kernel OOM (timestamp + logs link), adjusted route X throttle, pinned route Y to v2.1-quant.
- followups: Samir to re-evaluate quant variant registry (PR #452), Alex to review node-level OOM trend.
- my contact: paged via Slack if needed in first 30m after handoff.

If this doc is useful, I should convert to a formal runbook and link to Confluence. For now: shorthand and messy, but workable.

-- Maya
